messages.subject: crates/n8n-node-model: INode drops unknown fields, so a real workflow cannot round-trip through the Rust model

payload.finding: crates/n8n-node-model/src/lib.rs models INode with id, name, type, typeVersion, position, parameters, disabled only. A real workflow JSON also carries credentials, onError, notes, notesInFlow, retryOnFail, maxTries, waitBetweenTries, alwaysOutputData, executeOnce, webhookId, continueOnFail, and future fields; serde drops every one of them, so parse -> serialize loses data before crates/n8n-workflow ever sees it.
payload.requested_change: Add a passthrough to INode, e.g. #[serde(flatten)] pub extra: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> (or model the full field set). Same treatment for INodeParameters if it stays an opaque wrapper. This mirrors what the reference guarantees: `INode` is an open interface (interfaces.ts) and n8n persists unknown fields verbatim.
payload.why_now: The Workflow port's R1 step (document <-> aggregate conversion) needs a lossless INode; without it the Rust Workflow cannot round-trip a workflow JSON, which is the first thing n8n does on load/save.
payload.evidence: docs/isolation/workflow-rust-port-review.md §2.1 and §2.5; reference: interfaces.ts L1297-1335 (INode), tests/reference/workflow-rust/fixtures.json (checksum + toJSON sections pin the array/keyed shapes)

messages.subject: crates/n8n-connection: get_connected_nodes is a different function than the reference, and compareConnections (frozen surface #15) is missing

payload.finding_1: crates/n8n-connection::get_connected_nodes(connections, source_node) flattens every connection type and every output slot, has no depth parameter, and iterates a HashMap (non-deterministic order).
